[Reconstructed from YouGov .sav labels; not the fielded instrument] Asked about each of six contacts the respondent named: three close contacts ("From time to time, most people discuss important matters with others. Value for the contact this headline was attributed to. "Close/distant contacts believe claims" (check all contacts who believe each claim). Claims: Joe Biden is a socialist; The 2020 election was stolen by the Democrats; Covid-19 vaccines modify your DNA; A new world order - elites who control the media, industry, and government - were implicated in most wars over the last 200 years; Trump is still president of the United States; Republicans want to end Social Security and Medicare

[Reconstructed from YouGov .sav labels; not the fielded instrument] "Trusted political news sources": mean of six items (Family and friends; WhatsApp groups; Social media; Conservative media; Liberal media; Spanish-language media), 1 = Distrust ... 5 = Trust.

[Reconstructed from YouGov .sav labels; not the fielded instrument] Information type: True/neutral. Each conjoint profile shows one headline, attributed to one of the respondent's six named contacts; the headline (and so its information type) is randomly drawn from 80 headlines (21 of this type), in English or Spanish. Example headlines: How to improve your sleep quality | Exercise reduces cortisol levels | The benefits of meditation and mindfulness

[Reconstructed from YouGov .sav labels; not the fielded instrument] Information type: Misinformation. Each conjoint profile shows one headline, attributed to one of the respondent's six named contacts; the headline (and so its information type) is randomly drawn from 80 headlines (29 of this type), in English or Spanish. Example headlines: George Soros has endorsed (Ron) DeSantis for 2024. | Biden proposes record budget of 6.8 trillion dollars to win against Russia

[Reconstructed from YouGov .sav labels; not the fielded instrument] Information type: Fact-check. Each conjoint profile shows one headline, attributed to one of the respondent's six named contacts; the headline (and so its information type) is randomly drawn from 80 headlines (30 of this type), in English or Spanish. Example headlines: No, Tucker Carlson didn't say Ukraine is staging dead bodies | GOP wants a '30% tax on everything'? That ignores taxes that would end, bill's limited chances
